subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should non-local device-less shared-token WebSocket clients be allowed to retain operator scopes, and if so only through a bounded configured policy such as `gateway.auth.tokenScopes`?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the requested behavior changes who can obtain `operator.write`/`operator.admin` over a network token-auth connection, so automation should not choose the permanent auth boundary.

options.title: Use bounded configured scopes
options.body: Land or refine the `gateway.auth.tokenScopes` style approach so trusted deployments can opt into static scopes with non-loopback safeguards, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Restore requested scopes directly
options.body: Allow valid shared-token clients to keep self-declared scopes, accepting a wider trust model for any holder of the shared token.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed policy
options.body: Treat the current clearing behavior as intentional and close the bug only after documenting the required device-identity or configured-scope path.

recommendation.title: Use bounded configured scopes
recommendation.body: Land or refine the `gateway.auth.tokenScopes` style approach so trusted deployments can opt into static scopes with non-loopback safeguards, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the overlapping open token-scopes PR and introduced the current extracted Gateway connect-policy structure.
